heroText: Cairo is Egypt's ancient-meets-modern megacity, sprawling along the Nile beside the Giza Pyramids and Sphinx just across the river. First-time visitors should explore the Egyptian Museum for pharaonic treasures, wander the historic lanes of Khan el-Khalili bazaar, and walk the Islamic Cairo district around the Citadel of Saladin. Cairo International Airport connects the city to destinations across the world.

areas.name: Zamalek
areas.text: Zamalek is a leafy island district on the Nile known for embassies, galleries and cafes, a calm, walkable base close to central Cairo.

areas.name: Downtown Cairo
areas.text: Downtown Cairo centres on early 20th-century boulevards near Tahrir Square, close to the Egyptian Museum and many budget-to-mid-range hotels.

areas.name: Giza
areas.text: Giza sits beside the Pyramids and Sphinx on the Nile's west bank, the practical base for pyramid views and early morning visits.

areas.name: New Cairo
areas.text: New Cairo is a modern, spread-out suburb east of the centre with newer hotels, malls and easy airport access.
areas.bestFor: business trips, modern amenities, airport access

airports.name: Cairo International Airport (CAI)
airports.text: Cairo International Airport lies northeast of downtown; traffic can be heavy, so budget 45 minutes to over an hour depending on time of day.

airportTransfer.value: Compare road transfer time between Cairo International Airport (CAI) and central Cairo before choosing an airport-area or city-centre hotel.

stayOverview: Base in Zamalek for a calm, leafy stay near central sights, or Downtown Cairo for budget-friendly access to the Egyptian Museum and Tahrir Square. Giza suits travellers prioritizing the Pyramids, while New Cairo offers modern hotels near the airport.
hotelIntro: Cairo hotel choice depends on priorities: Zamalek and Downtown put museums and central sights within reach, Giza keeps the Pyramids and Sphinx just minutes away, and New Cairo suits business travellers wanting modern amenities and easier airport access.
rentalCars: A rental car isn't recommended in Cairo's dense traffic; use the Cairo Metro, ride-hailing apps or a hired driver instead.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Zamalek or Downtown Cairo for central sightseeing, or Giza if the Pyramids are the priority for your stay.

travelTips.title: Getting around
travelTips.text: Use the Cairo Metro for fast cross-city trips and ride-hailing apps for door-to-door journeys, since traffic can be unpredictable.

travelTips.title: Pyramid visits
travelTips.text: Visit the Giza Pyramids early in the morning to avoid both the heat and the largest crowds later in the day.

travelTips.title: Bazaar bargaining
travelTips.text: Expect to negotiate prices at Khan el-Khalili and other markets, where initial asking prices are usually well above the expected sale price.

history.label: 4th century
history.text: Around the turn of the fourth century, as Memphis was continuing to decline in importance, the Romans established a large fortress along the east bank of the Nile.
In 641 or early 642, after the surrender of Alexandria, the Egyptian capital at the time, he founded a new settlement next to Babylon Fortress.
In 750, following the overthrow of the Umayyad Caliphate by the Abbasids, the new rulers created their own settlement to the northeast of Fustat which became the new provincial capital.
Between 1087 and 1092 Badr al-Gamali also rebuilt the city walls in stone and constructed the city gates of Bab al-Futuh, Bab al-Nasr, and Bab Zuweila that still stand today.
